Marriage has lots of legal consequences:

  • For the purposes of real property, the "marital unit" can own property as a single entity, as opposed to two individual owners.
  • Marriage is a privileged relationship, which means that communications between spouses are protected from testimonial disclosure and spouses do not have to testify against/condemn the other spouse.
  • When it comes to wills and trusts, there are rules of inheritance where the surviving spouse will have title to the others possessions if they die without a will.
  • You need the state (aka government) to enforce these rights through the courts.

I also think that the tax benefits of marriage are justified. In the eyes of the law, marriage is two individuals becoming one unit, so it makes sense that they can combine their incomes and are taxed as that unit, as opposed to individually. This seems to meet the realities of marriage where the couple combines finances and makes collective decisions on spending, housing, and leisure.
